title: Windows Calculator: UWP to WinUI 3 migration report
migration: UWP + WinUI 2 to WinUI 3 (Windows App SDK 2.6.5, .NET 8, MSIX); C#/WinRT 2.3.1 for the C++/WinRT CalcManager.Interop component
tooling: winui-migrate 0.2.4 from C:\phase2\winui-tools, local branch user/raghavmadan/temp-native-winrt-components (commits b074b99, dcfee29, fc3f7df, 46b9c43, e66abc4; not pushed)
note: The user asked the agent to fix the harness and keep working until the migrated app launches, and was not available for approval prompts. The agent approved assessment revisions on that directive. Every decision answer is the same as the one the user approved for the first run. After the first launch the agent fixed six runtime problems the evaluators cannot see (E19-E24) and checked the app with UI Automation, comparing doubtful behaviour with the installed UWP Calculator.

agentEdits.change: Removed the carried <Compile Include="**\*.cs" /> from the two converted test/view-model projects, exactly as the fixed converter now writes them.
agentEdits.reason: The copy was converted by the engine before fix dcfee29; retarget treats an SDK-style project as done, so the fix would not be re-applied to it.

agentEdits.area: Graphing mode left out (consequence of D3 exclude-scope)
agentEdits.change: Removed the GraphControl project references; excluded the graphing views, view models, EquationTextBox, MathRichEditBox, KeyGraphFeaturesTemplateSelector and GraphingViewModelTests from compilation; removed MathRichEditBoxStyle from App.xaml; MainPage no longer creates the graphing view and shows the Graphing item disabled; startup falls back to Standard if Graphing is requested; the jump list skips Graphing.
agentEdits.reason: GraphControl is C++/CX, which WinUI 3 cannot host. The harness leaves exclude-scope subjects to be removed by hand. Porting GraphControl to C++/WinRT is a large change that needs the owner.

agentEdits.change: CommunityToolkit.Uwp.Controls.SettingsControls 8.2.251219 replaced by CommunityToolkit.WinUI.Controls.SettingsControls 8.2.251219, the same toolkit release built for WinUI 3. Settings.xaml already uses its namespace (CommunityToolkit.WinUI.Controls).
agentEdits.reason: The harness has no rule for this package and D16 was deferred; the UWP package pulls in UWP XAML types (NETSDK1218).

agentEdits.change: Restored the original conditions on the two AppxManifest items (release manifest only when UseReleaseAppxManifest is True), as the converter now writes them.
agentEdits.reason: The converter dropped ItemGroup conditions, so both manifests applied together (APPX1502). Fixed in the harness; the copy was converted before the fix.

agentEdits.area: Graphing mode left out (consequence of D3 exclude-scope)
agentEdits.change: Deleted the graphing-only source files that were already excluded from compilation (Views\GraphingCalculator, Calculator.ViewModels\GraphingCalculator, EquationTextBox.cs, MathRichEditBox.cs, KeyGraphFeaturesTemplateSelector.cs, GraphingViewModelTests.cs) and the Compile/Page Remove items that excluded them.
agentEdits.reason: The runtime and windowing evaluators scan every .cs file under a project folder, including files the project removes from compilation, so 7 findings in code that is never built kept those checks failing. They remain in the original repository for a later graphing port.

agentEdits.change: OnLaunched now takes Microsoft.UI.Xaml.LaunchActivatedEventArgs and reads protocol (ms-calculator:snapshot) activation from AppInstance.GetActivatedEventArgs; the OnActivated override, splash-screen wait and prelaunch branch are gone (the jump list is set up after activation). Startup sizing keeps its first-launch condition and DIP semantics through OverlappedPresenter.PreferredMinimum* and AppWindow.ResizeClient scaled by the window DPI. The Suspending work (button-usage log, always-on-top size) runs on the primary window's AppWindow.Closing, per decision D8 (a). The UWP user ID is no longer available and only fed the graphing policy.
agentEdits.reason: WinUI 3 has no OnActivated, SplashScreen, ApplicationView or Suspending; the loop reported these as MissingCapability (lifecycle and view sizing) with no registered recipe.

agentEdits.change: The custom title bar uses the owning window: Window.ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar and SetTitleBar, AppWindow.TitleBar insets and height (physical pixels converted to DIPs), AppWindow.Changed instead of IsVisibleChanged/LayoutMetricsChanged, AppWindowTitleBar for the caption-button colours, UIViewSettingsInterop.GetForWindow for the interaction mode, the WinUI WindowActivatedEventArgs, and DispatcherQueue instead of the null CoreDispatcher.
agentEdits.reason: CoreApplicationView title-bar behaviour has no registered recipe (WINUI0011 / ApplicationView colours through a field); the windowing skill requires preserving the custom title bar rather than replacing it with a template.

agentEdits.change: KeyboardShortcutManager listens to the main page's routed KeyDown, KeyUp and CharacterReceived events (including already-handled ones) instead of CoreWindow events; Alt-chord navigation moved from AcceleratorKeyActivated to the key-up with the menu key down; modifier state comes from InputKeyboardSource.GetKeyStateForCurrentThread.
agentEdits.reason: Window.CoreWindow is null in a desktop window, so the old registration would throw when the main page is created.

agentEdits.change: ApplicationViewModel receives its AppWindow from the page and switches between the CompactOverlay and Default presenters, restoring the saved custom size in DIPs; a shared Utils.ToPhysicalSize helper converts DIP sizes with the window DPI. Window IDs for logging use the existing Utils.GetWindowId (-1 for the single desktop window) instead of GetApplicationViewIdForWindow(CoreWindow).
agentEdits.reason: ApplicationView.GetForCurrentView and the CoreWindow-based view ID throw in a desktop process; the view-model project cannot reach App.MainWindow, so the page supplies the window instead of a new global.

agentEdits.change: ResourceLoader.GetForViewIndependentUse/GetForCurrentView became MRT Core ResourceLoader (default map and the CEngineStrings map); the RTL check reads LayoutDirection from an MRT Core resource context with the app language as fallback, and the currency loader no longer needs a CoreWindow to ask.
agentEdits.reason: Current-view resource factories have no registered recipe; decision D12 (a) asked for an MRT Core context that keeps the qualifier the app reads.

agentEdits.change: Settings no longer registers with SystemNavigationManager; its existing in-app Back button gains GoBack and Alt+Left keyboard accelerators.
agentEdits.reason: Decision D13 (a): use existing in-app navigation; a desktop window has no system back button.

agentEdits.area: Runtime hazards the evaluators do not flag
agentEdits.change: Dispatcher.RunAsync calls became DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue (main page, calculator view, title bar, unit converter callbacks); the display-size query uses DisplayInformationInterop.GetForWindow; Timeline/Recall activity requests use the documented IUserActivityRequestManagerInterop.GetForWindow, guarded so a failure is logged rather than stopping launch; PointerDeviceType comparisons use Microsoft.UI.Input; leftover m_graphingCalculator references from the graphing cut were removed.
agentEdits.reason: These compile in WinUI 3 but return null or throw at run time (or no longer compile once earlier errors cleared), and none of them is reported by the runtime-compatibility evaluator.

agentEdits.change: The 69 tile and splash images that only Microsoft's internal Store build supplies are back under the original ItemGroup Condition="'$(IsStoreBuild)' == 'True'".
agentEdits.reason: This project was converted before harness fix fc3f7df kept ItemGroup conditions, and the loop does not reconvert a converted project; the open-source build failed packaging with 69 APPX0702 missing-payload errors.

agentEdits.change: Non-Store builds set AppxDefaultResourceQualifierUAP_AlternateForm=colorful, so the colorful splash images (the only non-high-contrast ones in the open-source assets) become the PRI default.
agentEdits.reason: Windows refused to register the package: the splash screen had no default or neutral candidate (0x80073B06). Verified by registering a layout with the changed index; the tiles' missing defaults do not block registration.

agentEdits.change: TitleBar and MainPage use Microsoft.UI.System.ThemeSettings created for the main window (HighContrast and Changed) instead of AccessibilitySettings.HighContrastChanged; MainPage acts only when the high-contrast state actually changes and runs on the UI thread.
agentEdits.reason: Subscribing to AccessibilitySettings.HighContrastChanged needs a CoreWindow and threw 0x80070490 (Element not found) from TitleBar.OnLoaded, crashing the app at startup. The runtime-compatibility evaluator does not flag this API.

agentEdits.change: The main window is titled with the app's display name (DevAppName, or AppName in a Store build), as UWP titled the view.
agentEdits.reason: A desktop window otherwise shows the default "WinUI Desktop" in the taskbar and Alt+Tab.

agentEdits.change: TitleBar.OnUnloaded unsubscribes from the AppWindow only while the window still has one.
agentEdits.reason: A closing Window has already released its AppWindow. It compiles cleanly and only happens on close; the launch check watches start-up and no evaluator closes the window normally.
agentEdits.problem: Closing the window crashed the app (NullReferenceException in TitleBar.OnUnloaded). Every UI test class in run 108056 ended in this crash.

agentEdits.change: AppResourceProvider trims the key and returns an empty string when the resource map has no such key, as the UWP ResourceLoader did; a loader that failed to construct keeps its existing fallback.
agentEdits.reason: MRT Core's ResourceLoader.GetString throws for a missing key and does not ignore spaces around it. The UWP loader returned an empty string and resolved upstream's two 'MillimeterOfMercury ' keys (trailing space since the first open-source commit); the installed UWP Calculator 11.2502 lists 'Millimeters of mercury'. Runtime-only, and no evaluator opens a converter.
agentEdits.problem: Opening any unit converter threw COMException 0x80073B17 (named resource not found) from the navigation handler. After the first version of this fix, the Pressure unit 'Millimeters of mercury' still showed a blank name.

agentEdits.change: The GoBack keyboard accelerator on the Settings back button is created in code; Alt+Left stays in markup.
agentEdits.reason: WinUI 3 markup cannot convert "GoBack" to a VirtualKey. The XAML compiles and fails only when the page loads; no evaluator navigates to Settings.
agentEdits.problem: The Settings page failed to load (XamlParseException), so Settings could not be opened.

agentEdits.area: Window size and position on relaunch
agentEdits.problem: From the second launch on, the window opened at a large system default size (about 1080 x 618) instead of where it was last closed.
agentEdits.change: A small WindowPlacement helper tracks the main window's last normal position, size and maximized state, saves it to local settings on close and restores it on later launches, kept on a display that still exists. Always-on-top pauses the tracking so its compact size is not saved as the normal one. The first launch keeps the compact default size.
agentEdits.reason: UWP's PreferredLaunchWindowingMode.Auto reopened a view at its last size and position; a desktop window does not, and the converted comment assumed it did. Nothing in the loop relaunches the app, and the windowing skill has no recipe for it.

agentEdits.problem: Each time always-on-top was entered, the mini window came back one title bar (31 DIP) taller.
agentEdits.change: Utils.SetClientSize gives the window an exact client size by measuring its frame, and the always-on-top size is saved as that client size (Utils.GetClientSizeInDips) instead of Window.Bounds or the page size. The mini window is the UWP 320 x 394 view size, title bar included, every time.
agentEdits.reason: AppWindow.ResizeClient adds a standard caption, but this window's content extends into the title bar, so the saved and restored sizes disagreed. It only shows across repeated always-on-top round trips, which no evaluator performs.

agentEdits.problem: Choosing Logical shift, Rotate circular or Rotate through carry in Programmer mode did nothing: the flyout stayed open and the arithmetic shift buttons stayed.
agentEdits.change: LshLogicalButton sets its keyboard character, auditory feedback and accessible name with the same ResourceString lookups as its neighbours instead of x:Uid.
agentEdits.reason: Its x:Uid resources include a [using:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation]AutomationProperties.Name key, and WinUI 3 did not load this lazily loaded button. The mode handler returns early while any of the six deferred shift buttons is missing, so every shift mode stopped working. It is the app's only x:Uid with an old-namespace key; the other 228 old-namespace keys are read by name through the app's ResourceString extension and work. No evaluator opens the bit-shift flyout.

compromises.detail: Not available in the WinUI 3 build. The nav item is shown disabled. GraphControl (C++/CX + DirectX, about 4,500 lines) needs a C++/WinRT port on Microsoft.UI.Xaml to bring it back. The open-source build only had a mock graphing engine.

MainPage's WinUI 2 BackdropMaterial was removed under decision D6 (option a), so the window uses the default background. Setting Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.MicaBackdrop as the window's SystemBackdrop would bring Mica back.

The converted project dropped the original's conditional PropertyGroups, including the IsStoreBuild DefineConstants (SEND_DIAGNOSTICS;IS_STORE_BUILD). Developer builds are unaffected; a Store build needs them added back. Not verified here.
DisplayInformationInterop.GetForWindow returns E_NOTIMPL for a desktop window, so the 'under 7 inches, portrait' layout rule never applies; it only mattered on phones.

buildAndLaunch.note: First by the harness in run 108056: winapp registered the Debug x64 build and the launch evaluator saw the window 'Calculator [Dev]'. Before it, the agent's throwaway builds (temporary patches, restored afterwards) found the registration failure and start-up crash fixed by E15-E17. Run 7a761d repeated the launch with no repairs.

testMethod: After the first launch, on clean Debug x64 builds (no diagnostic code) registered with 'winapp run --no-build --no-launch' and started from shell:AppsFolder: UI Automation from Windows PowerShell 5.1 (Invoke, SelectionItem, Toggle, Transform and Window patterns), WM_CLOSE for a normal close, and the Application event log for crash events. Behaviour that looked different was compared with the installed UWP Windows Calculator 11.2502, built from the same open-source code but still using the older C++ view model. Synthesized keyboard and mouse input is denied in this session, so the WinAppDriver suite cannot pass here. The remote desktop session was disconnected during the checks: screenshots after that are black and the installed UWP Calculator stopped responding to UI Automation, so the last screenshot with content is from 14:13 UTC (run 7a761d build). UI Automation's WindowPattern.Close returned an error and left the port's window open (the installed UWP Calculator closed this way); not investigated. E19-E21 were found with a temporarily instrumented build that logged first-chance and unhandled exceptions and binding failures, restored afterwards.

notBugs: The unit drop-downs on converter pages have no accessible name. The original source's C# view model sets Unit1AutomationName and Unit2AutomationName only when units are swapped; the installed Calculator, still on the older C++ view model, names them 'Input unit' and 'Output unit'.

228 resource keys per language still say [using:Windows.UI.Xaml.Automation] or [using:Windows.UI.Xaml.Controls]. The app reads them by name through its ResourceString extension, so they still work: button names match the installed Calculator ('Clear', 'Seven', 'Plus', 'Memory store', 'Keep on top'). The one key reached through x:Uid was the E24 problem.
RolCarryButton's automation ID is 'rolButton' in the original XAML too.
About 43 handled first-chance exceptions at start-up come from engine strings the CEngineStrings resources never had; they resolve to empty text, as on UWP.
takeaways: MRT Core's ResourceLoader.GetString throws for a missing key and does not trim the key; UWP returned an empty string and tolerated surrounding spaces.
A desktop window does not reopen where it was closed; UWP's PreferredLaunchWindowingMode.Auto behaviour needs explicit persistence.
AppWindow.ResizeClient adds a standard caption even when content extends into the title bar; set client sizes by measuring the frame.
An x:Uid whose resources use [using:Windows.UI.Xaml.*] attached-property keys stopped a lazily loaded element from loading in WinUI 3; rewrite such keys to Microsoft.UI.Xaml or drop the x:Uid.
WinUI 3 markup rejects KeyboardAccelerator Key="GoBack"; Window.AppWindow is null while a Window closes.
AccessibilitySettings.HighContrastChanged throws without a CoreWindow; Microsoft.UI.System.ThemeSettings replaces it.
A package needs a neutral (default) splash-screen resource to register.
Removing BackdropMaterial needs a replacement backdrop (Window.SystemBackdrop = MicaBackdrop); without one the window is black in every theme and Light theme is unreadable.
outcome: Builds, registers and launches; calculator modes, bit shift, converters, Settings, always-on-top, relaunch placement and a clean close checked with UI Automation. 120/123 required checks: the unit-test host and the UI test run remain open.

timeNote: Agent usage comes from this Copilot CLI session's local usage store (claude-opus-5.5), split at the first successful launch (13:28:28 UTC, run 108056); snapshot at 15:20 UTC, so the last report-refresh steps are not included. Input tokens include cache reads (182.9M before the launch, 57.5M after); fresh input was 3.78M before and 0.43M after. Premium requests are the sum of request multipliers. Active minutes add up gaps under 10 minutes between model calls, so waiting on harness runs and idle time are excluded. The migration row is all agent: loop steering (assessments, decision answers, approvals) was not separated from harness work and direct edits, so the agent share is an upper bound and the loop share a lower bound. Wall time: 06:45 to 15:20 UTC (about 8.6 hours).
